facts.text: Lycoming grew around the Rome, Watertown and Ogdensburg Railroad, becoming the town’s only station and boosting local fruit and dairy markets.
The town’s name honors George Scriba, a Dutch merchant who owned over 499,000 acres as partial repayment of debts owed by the Roosevelt family in the 1790s.
Lycoming sits about 6 miles east of Oswego, near Lake Ontario’s southern shore, and is part of the Syracuse metropolitan area.
The hamlet’s first post office, operated by Coe, now functions only as a PO Box, reflecting Lycoming’s quiet rural character.
Early settlers cleared forests along Black Creek and Nine Mile Creek, turning the fertile sandy loam soils into productive farms for grain, livestock, and milling.
